The swing reference is rebuilt through the live stance pose every tick, so the stance origin is already absent from the residual, and between the last pre-commit solve and touchdown the stance chart moves \(4\) mm or less — against landing errors of \(32\)–\(134\) mm. The placement loop is already closed by replanning at 50 Hz, not by the choice of task frame.
  • The gain is real but not decisive. About \(15\) mm at September baseline settings, against the \(51.6\) mm lateral periodic offset of (6.8) — roughly \(30\%\) of the lateral scale. The justification is that it is nearly free: a reference-law change on an existing task, no Jacobian change, no new task type, no new failure mode. Not that \(15\) mm settles anything.

docs.title: 12.7) Hard/soft designation is an executor mode
docs.text:
\(p_f = p_{k+1}\) and \(p_f - c^-_{k+1} = r^{TD}_k\) cannot both hold when the body is not where predicted. Designating which is hard does not remove the trade-off; it relocates the decision to one named place instead of burying it in a trajectory blend.

mode terminal knot fails by use on com-hard \(r^{TD}_k\), per (12.2) world landing drifts flat, slippery, compliant world-hard \(R_{CW}(p_{k+1} - \hat c(t))\), recomputed each tick CoM estimate error enters placement stones, stair edges

One bit on the executor, switchable per step. The rationale is terrain-driven: landing off a stone is unrecoverable, so world position is hard there; on flat ground world position is unconstrained while leg geometry is not; on slippery or compliant ground the world foothold estimate is the unreliable quantity.

A blend is rejected. An earlier proposal interpolated two coordinate trajectories with a weight \(\beta(t)\). It was rejected because \(\beta\) had no owner and interacted badly with replanning and retiming — the same reason the capture/viability split in Section 3.3 is a split rather than a weighting.

docs.title: 13.1) Swing task frame: a three-way trade
docs.text:
The world linear Jacobian of a frame \(F\) on a floating base is

\[ J_F = \big[\; I_3 ,\;\; -[\,p_F - p_{\text{base}}\,]_\times ,\;\; J_{F,\text{joints}} \;\big], \tag{13.1} \]

so any relative position task in a captured chart has \(J_{\text{rel}} = R_{CW}(J_b - J_a)\), in which the base translation columns always cancel. What differs between frames is everything else:

foot-to-foot (September baseline) base-to-foot CoM-to-foot (chosen) joint columns both legs swing leg only both legs, arms, torso cross-limb Hessian block nonzero exactly zero nonzero attitude lever \(\approx 0.2\)–\(0.5\) m \(\approx 0.95\) m \(\approx 0.86\) m Hessian pattern static static configuration-dependent matches the planner's variable no — needs a conversion no yes, exactly CoM motion enters as an ALIP feedforward an ALIP feedforward the Jacobian, exactly

Base-to-foot is the best structural answer and is not chosen. Setting \(a = \text{base}\) leaves \(J_{\text{foot,joints}}\) alone: the stance-leg columns are exactly zero and the two limbs are independent in the QP. But it does not match the planner's decision variable, so it still needs a conversion, and it pays the full attitude lever for a decoupling property this planner does not need.

The attitude lever is the accepted cost. Foot-to-foot is differentially immune to base rotation, because both feet swing together about the base and the effect largely cancels in the difference; neither anchored form is. At \(0.86\) m a \(0.5\) rad/s base pitch rate injects \(0.43\) m/s into the residual, against roughly \(0.15\) m/s for the same rate at a \(0.3\) m step separation. The swing task therefore becomes a competitor for base angular authority, which is already contested: an upper-body envelope that clamps base yaw dumps the residual into a single foot corner, with an eightfold spin reduction when disabled.

Why CoM-to-foot wins anyway. The planner decides \(r_k = p_{k+1} - c^-\). Only the CoM-relative task tracks that quantity with the correct Jacobian. Every other frame requires CoM motion to enter as a feedforward computed from the ALIP, and Section 2.7 measured that model drifting about \(96\%\) of the invariant's own mean within a step. Given a choice between a wrong feedforward in the 1 kHz loop and a well-conditioned-but-coupled Jacobian, this formulation takes the Jacobian.

If the gate of Section 17 shows the attitude coupling costs more than the feedforward error, the reference-law route of Section 12.2 is the documented fallback and needs no planner change.

docs.title: 13.2) Timing representations
docs.text:
Section 4.2 reduced the problem to "how to represent a known 1-D curve in a convex program." The candidates:

# representation added integers model error leak 1 conic, Section 4 \(16\) linear rows no \(\mathbf{0.23}\) mm one side, diagnosed 2 SOS2 piecewise, \(20\) ms lattice \(K\) vars + SOS2 yes \(0.148\) mm none 3 SOS1 one-hot \(\equiv\) the outer grid \(K\) vars + \(K\) binaries yes \(0\) at lattice, \(7.4\) mm quantization none 4 reciprocal sandwich \((\varsigma,\mu)\) \(2\) vars + \(J{+}1\) rows no \(3.7\) mm at \(\pm50\) ms both sides, bounded 5 relinearized QP + trust region \(1\) var + \(2\) rows no \(3.9\) mm at \(\pm50\) ms deterministic 6 outer grid, \(5\)–\(15\) solves none enumerated \(0\) none

#3 is worse than it looks. Since \(\dot\ell = \lambda q\), a \(20\) ms quantum is \(\lambda q^- \times 0.02 = 14.9\) mm of \(\ell\) at \(q^- = 0.22\) m — a \(7.4\) mm half-quantum resolution loss, larger than #1's and #2's model error. Discretizing \(T\) is not free merely because the planner ticks at \(20\) ms.

#2 is the documented escalation from #1, using the same variables: it forces the point onto the piecewise chord of the curve rather than anywhere above it, and at \(20\) ms spacing the chord error is \(0.148\) mm. Since stepping stones already need region binaries (Section 9), timing then becomes the same kind of decision in one MIQP. The trigger is a persistently nonzero \(g_k\) from (4.9).

#4 and #5 have the same error curve. Both are second-order accurate on the same smooth function, so curvature governs, not the device. They were the initial proposal and are superseded by #1.

#6 is what #1 replaces. Five to fifteen inner solves per tick, each giving a true inner optimum, refined by bisection. It is correct and trivially parallelizable; it is rejected on solve budget, not on accuracy.

docs.title: 13.3) Branches rejected outright
docs.text:
• Geometric programming in log coordinates. \(\ln\xi\) and \(\ln(-\zeta)\) are both affine in \(T\), which is tempting. Dead end: \(q = (\xi - |\zeta|)/2\) and \(\ell = (\xi + |\zeta|)/2\) are differences of positive terms, so the constraints are signomial, not posynomial.
  • Plain convex hull of sampled durations (simplex weights, no SOS2). The hull of points on a convex curve is a lens whose lower boundary is the piecewise chord, within \(0.148\) mm — but the solver may land anywhere in its interior, up to the global chord gap. SOS2 is exactly the constraint that pins it to the lower boundary.
  • Free-final-time / time-scaling (\(dt = T\,ds\)). Bilinear in \((T,x)\) with no redemption, because the system is already linear so the reparameterization buys nothing.
  • Relax-then-project: solve with \(\ell^-\) free and project onto the hyperbola afterwards. Loses the optimality certificate, and the margin \(m_k\) of (3.9) becomes meaningless.

docs.title: 13.4) Orbital energy: monitor with it, do not optimize in it
docs.text:
The quantity \(E := \tfrac12 v^2 - \tfrac12\lambda^2 q^2\) is conserved within a step and factors as \(E = -\tfrac{\lambda^2}{2}\,\xi\zeta\) — so orbital energy and the divergent coordinate are the same geometry in different coordinates, with the level sets \(\xi\zeta = \text{const}\) being hyperbolas whose asymptotes are the \(\xi\) and \(\zeta\) lines. \(E > 0\): the CoM crosses over the foot. \(E < 0\): it stalls and reverses. \(E = 0\): the separatrices — both of them, which is exactly the ambiguity Section 4.4 guards against.

Touchdown is an energy reset, \(E_{k+1} = \tfrac12 (v^-_k)^2 - \tfrac12\lambda^2 r_k^2\), so a desired energy could in principle be commanded by \(|r_k| = \lambda^{-1}\sqrt{(v^-_k)^2 - 2E^{\text{des}}}\). It should not be:

touchdown-relative form energy form dependence on \(r_k\) affine quadratic, nonconvex direction / side information preserved destroyed (through \(r^2\)) composition over \(N\) steps linear recursion nested radicals lateral period-2 gait natural awkward scalar speed invariant via the orbit direct

Formulate in \(r_k\); monitor in \(E\). Energy is the right quantity for a scalar gait-health monitor, a terrain-independent speed interface, and reasoning about unplanned events — a push is naturally an energy perturbation, and the hyperbola picture says how much placement absorbs it. It is the wrong quantity inside the QP.

A useful classifier that falls out of the same geometry: the CoM-over-foot instant

\[ T_0 = \frac{1}{\lambda}\operatorname{artanh}\!\left(-\frac{q(\tilde t)}{\ell(\tilde t)}\right), \qquad \text{which exists in forward time}\iff \xi(\tilde t) > 0, \]

solving \(q(T_0) = 0\) in (1.4). The condition says the divergent coordinate is ahead of the stance foot — equivalently, that the robot will actually pass over its foot rather than stall and reverse. That makes \(T_0\) a useful walking / stalling classifier. It is not the minimizer of any placement requirement, and an earlier draft that claimed so was wrong.

docs.title: 14) Implementation checklist
docs.text:
This is the current implementation reading path, not a request to install the earlier CoP/bias proposals.

  1. Read the app profile. Use the resolved ALIP, coordinator and reference settings; derivation fixtures are not defaults.
  2. Capture the support chart. Digit latches the support foot-link position and planner heading, then forms measured CoM displacement and scaled contact angular momentum in that chart.
  3. Supply the model height. The app latches its solve-facing height; zero kernel input selects the configured fallback height.
  4. Assemble shared timing. Both axes use the same exponential timing variables. Apply duration, optional retiming and geometry bounds before propagation.
  5. Solve and postcheck. Evaluate exact first-step flow and hard geometry. Distinguish nominal, recovery, degraded, failed and held outputs; never infer physical safety from a solver success or certified alone.
  6. Honor plan lifetime. A held plan is valid only within the same support identity. The coordinator requests timing and owns touchdown, preparation and commitment.
  7. Author and acknowledge delivery. The app builds continuous task futures and binary activation targets, records preview timing, and uses Servo acknowledgement for admission replay.
  8. Validate the integrated behavior. Inspect tracking, contact, completion and termination in the owning app. Reduced-model parity is not physical acceptance.

docs.title: 15.1) Allocation and solver
docs.text:
A single QP replaces the five to fifteen solves of the outer grid, so the per-tick budget is no longer the binding concern; allocation discipline still is.

  • Pre-size one workspace. Build the sparsity pattern once per \((N,\text{stance side})\): the conic tangent rows change coefficients but not structure between solves.
  • Audit with more than one counter. A single allocation counter has repeatedly proven insufficient, and PartialPivLU cannot be made allocation-free — plan around it rather than trying to eliminate it.
  • Do not call a full FK sweep for contact heights. A per-contact-name height query costs one whole kinematics sweep each; call forward_kinematics once, then use cached frame placements.
  • The abort criterion is 10 consecutive unsolved ticks, not one. A recoverable burst of about 21 ticks has been observed; aborting on the first failure converts a recoverable transient into a fall.
  • If no feasible point attains \(m \ge m\_{\min}\), that is a margin event, not a solver failure (Section 16).

docs.title: 15.2) Sign and unit discipline
docs.text:
Four places this formulation breaks quietly. Each gets a test, not a comment.

  1. The lateral scaled-momentum sign in (1.3). Assert with a test that integrates both axes from \((q,\ell) = (0.1,\,0)\) and requires identical results. Without the flip, magnitudes still match and only the closed loop fails.
  2. The conic branch (4.4). Classify from \(\operatorname{sign}\xi_0\) and \(\operatorname{sign}\zeta_0\), never from \(E_0\) alone; assert the classification against the measured state every solve.
  3. \(\alpha\_\ell\) is dimensionless, where the corresponding gain in a velocity formulation is in seconds. Any ported constant is wrong by a factor of \(\lambda\). Name it alpha_l in code, never alpha.
  4. \(\ell\) is a length. Log it in metres and log raw \(L\) in \(\mathrm{kg\,m^2/s}\) separately; do not let one channel carry both.

docs.title: 15.3) Chart and lifecycle
docs.text:
• \(R_{CW}\) is captured once per accepted step and never refreshed mid-step. A non-finite yaw is rejected without replacing the last valid capture, and reset clears it so a stale chart cannot cross a session.
  • The walk schedule is a motion clock. Latch its origin at the first walk mode entry, not at raw simulation time. Reading it at raw time breaks lateral walking specifically, which makes the resulting bug look unrelated to the clock.
  • gait_phase is a continuous non-decreasing state supplied by the step clock. The commit gate reads it; the swing author deliberately does not. Do not reintroduce elapsed / held_duration, which moves backward whenever an accepted plan lengthens the step.
  • No landing deadline. If touchdown admission does not fire, keep the cycle active and replan. A deadline plus a capture-region re-entry test is the lifecycle deadlock of Section 8.5: a bounce at speed produces no admission evidence, the coordinator drops to double support, and its only exit is a standing test a walking robot cannot pass.

docs.title: 15.4) Contact, CoP, and admission
docs.text:
Digit's planner replays the shared coordinator's full-rate contact history. Current admission requires capacity to have fallen to 0.50 after swing activation, then to reach 0.50 after 0.60 of the installed duration and persist for 5 ms. The shared-load exception is disabled. These app-profile values supersede the original proposal of a raw 100 N threshold held for 10 ms; the numerical ALIP kernel owns neither rule.

The pivot is the latched foot-link position, not a filtered allocation CoP. Force-derived channels remain evidence for investigating momentum balance; they are not a terrain-support oracle. The original flat/terrain closure measurements retain the limitations reported in Section 20.

docs.title: 15.5) Never evaluate ground closure on one channel
docs.text:
Under Section 12.1 no single task carries ground clearance. Any logic asking "how far above the ground is the foot" must read the difference of the two CoM-relative \(z\) channels, never either one alone:

\[ z_{\text{swing}} - z_{\text{stance}} = \big(z_{\text{swing}} - z_{\text{com}}\big) - \big(z_{\text{stance}} - z_{\text{com}}\big). \]

A single channel is CoM-referenced, and the CoM descends by design: a bounded coupled base descent ramps at \(0.25\) m/s, which over a \(0.44\) s swing is \(110\) mm of apparent swing descent that closes no gap with the ground. Phase, apex, descent-authority, touchdown-search and reach logic written on one channel will all fire early by exactly that amount.

Enforce with an assertion at the executor boundary, not a comment. The mirror failure is on record: an attempt that credited relative-frame depth read a rising stance as \(84\%\) swing progress, and was reverted.

docs.title: 15.6) Configuration surface
docs.text:
planner.rho                        successor pole; xi_des is DERIVED, eq. (6.4)
planner.conic_tangents             J, default 16
planner.margin_floor_m             m_min
planner.timing_soft_band_s         beta in (4.8)
planner.timing_slack_weight        w_T, exact penalty
planner.kg_mode                    none | measured | predicted
planner.momentum_bias.beta         corrector rate, eq. (5.2)
planner.momentum_bias.clamp
planner.exchange.v_closure_floor   0.1
planner.exchange.dt_max_s          0.1
control.foot_tasks.swing_weight    (w_x, w_y, w_z), CoM-relative swing role
control.foot_tasks.stance_weight_z scalar; the stance role emits no x/y rows
reference.swing_terminal_mode      com_hard | world_hard

Two repository facts that bite here:

  • Every walking tuning profile is read strictly. Since 2026-09-25 each file is read through config::ProfileReader: the keys read are the keys allowed and every key is required. A new key needs one read and a value in the September baseline profile; there is no allow-list to update.
  • Config tests assert contracts, not tuning. Band ordering, parity between left and right, the sign of mode-selecting knobs, and the (6.4) relation. Never pin a tuning magnitude.

docs.title: 15.7) Telemetry
docs.text:
Producers declare their own channels; there are no tiers; a declared-but-never-written channel is an enforced error; logs never depend on plotters.

plan/l_xy                     scaled momentum state, metres
plan/L_raw                    angular momentum about the contact, kg m^2/s
plan/k_G                      centroidal angular momentum, and kg_mode in use
plan/energy_xi0_zeta0         branch classifier inputs (never E0 alone)
plan/conic_gap                g_k of (4.9) -- zero means the cone is tight
plan/exchange_correction      the (2.5) term, per axis
plan/v_closure_z              the (5.3) denominator
plan/exchange_time_s          the (5.5) correction, signed
plan/timing_slack_s           s_T; nonzero means the soft band opened
plan/step_duration_s          T_1 recovered by (4.7)
plan/momentum_bias            delta_hat and the clamp flag
plan/margin_m                 m_k, signed, per preview node
plan/capture_index            N* = ceil(-ln(1-|xi|/B_x)/ln sigma);
                              stopping readiness only, never a walking gate
plan/capture_funnel_N         N_k of (8.1); absent outside the stopping mode
plan/pivot_source             cop | foot_link fallback

Report lateness as a lateral-viability quantity, per Section 5.6: pair plan/exchange_time_s with \(D^\star\) from (5.6), not with a fore-aft placement error, or the diagnostics will point at the wrong axis.

The log reader owns its schema list and two dialects are already live, so a new producer format tag without a matching reader entry presents as "no planner diagnostic block" rather than as a parse error — a failure mode worth recognizing on sight.

docs.title: 15.8) A/B discipline
docs.text:
• Build from a git archive copy when another session is editing the worktree, and pin the OpenMP cache variables. Prove binary identity by trajectories.
  • Dual-write both log paths in one process. Cross-run diffs show divergence, not defects.
  • A matching summary digest does not establish trajectory identity. An equal digest has survived a \(148\) mm divergence; prove inertness dataset by dataset against a pre-change binary.
  • Run bare ctest, not a filtered subset. The app suite gates on safety-state bookkeeping and a filter hides real regressions.

docs.title: 16) Failure semantics
docs.text:
condition classification response \(m_k < 0\) on the executed step margin event publish best-effort placement, report signed margin no feasible \(m \ge m_{\min}\) margin event maximize \(m\), flag \(g_k > 0\) on the executed step model degradation log; escalate to SOS2 if persistent postcheck disagrees with the QP model degradation reject the step, republish held plan, flag QP unsolved solver failure hold previous plan; abort only on 10 consecutive \(v_{\text{closure}}\) below floor model degradation \(\Delta t = 0\), flag; never divide contact wrench invalid pivot degradation fall back to the foot-link origin, flag \(k_G\) unavailable model degradation fall back to level 0, flag; do not silently zero unadmitted touchdown past \(T_1\) normal keep the cycle active and replan; no deadline non-finite chart yaw rejected keep the last valid capture; never fall back to live stance rotation

The distinction the table exists to enforce: a margin event is a quantified statement about the world, a solver failure is a statement about the optimization, and a model degradation is a statement about this document. They have different responses and must never share a status code.

docs.title: 17) Validation contract
docs.text:
The sequence below records the formulation's research gates and predictions, not a statement that every proposed experiment is pending or every criterion has passed. Use the kernel validation boundary and Digit validation for completed implementation checks and measured results.

Steps 1–3 are pure analysis on existing logs and change no code.

  1. Regress the four bias terms of Section 5.4 together — \(k_G\), pivot offset, effective ZMP, exchange correction — and resolve the \(31\) mm versus \(103\) mm discrepancy. The \(k_G\) term is already measured on flat and carries about half; this step is about the remaining half, and about whether the split holds on terrain.

This is the gate. If the residual is not attributable, the prediction is biased by an unmodelled term, and the margin of Section 3.4 — not the corrector of Section 5.5 — is what protects the gait.

  1. Publish \(v\_{\text{closure}}\) from the existing task \(z\) channel against the current planner. Zero risk. Prediction: reproduces the \(1.45\) ms/mm coefficient and exposes the stance roll-off term on terminal descent steps.
  2. Compute the exchange correction (2.5) offline across the terrain matrix. Prediction: zero on flat, a \(-0.13\) m/s scale on descent, and the two contributions opposing on descending stairs.
  3. CoM-relative foot tasks, planner unchanged. Convert the existing planner's foothold to a CoM-relative terminal condition and re-point the swing task. Log the attitude share \(\lVert \omega_{\text{base}} \times (p_{\text{foot}} - c) \rVert\) and the cross-limb Hessian coupling. Measure on up-stairs with flat as control. Prediction: stair tracking improves; flat holds or degrades, and any flat degradation correlates with base angular rate.

This is the controller gate. If flat degrades and the degradation is attitude-driven, the objection to anchored swing residuals still binds and the reference-law route of Section 12.2 is the fallback.

  1. The Section 7 QP, with the conic duration. Log plan/conic_gap from the first run; a persistently nonzero gap is the trigger for SOS2.
  2. Only then level-2 \(k_G\), if step 1 warrants it.

Required focused tests. Each targets a failure this document predicts:

test what it would catch two-axis integration identity (1.3)–(1.4) the lateral sign flip invariance of \(\xi\zeta\) along a simulated flow a wrong hyperbolic propagation conic branch classifier from \((\xi_0,\zeta_0)\) classifying from \(E_0\) alone the (6.4) \(\xi^{\mathrm{des}}\) relation a feedforward pinned in YAML invariant band (3.6) versus one-step capture band the silent regression of Section 3.2 the single-channel assertion of Section 15.5 ground closure read on one channel conic tangent gap at \(J = 16\) a polyhedron on the wrong side of the curve

Authority boundary. Dynamic authority is task traces and direct simulation runs. Unit tests cannot establish terrain or high-speed robustness, and no test above claims to. The corrector of Section 5.5 is inert on a steady orbit, so a test that holds the nominal gait measures nothing about it — validate it off-orbit and comparatively.

docs.title: 18) Scope boundary and non-goals
docs.text:
• No claim that this formulation fixes descending terrain. Section 1.1 models the gravitational moment arm exactly but not the contact-force profile, whose time variation matters over intervals as short as \(150\) ms and which a prior investigation established as necessary for the descent case. Sections 2.4 and 5.6 address two named terms — the exchange correction and touchdown timing — and nothing else.
  • No claim of improved slip or drift rejection. Section 12.6 settles it: the placement loop is already closed by replanning at 50 Hz, and the stance chart moves \(4\) mm or less over the frozen window.
  • No universal planner interface. The task set is planner-owned by design (Section 12.5); only the task types and the executor lifecycle are shared.
  • No external world-anchor task and no lone swing-foot Jacobian.
  • No terrain-normal frame and no terrain-height estimator.
  • No retuning of swing gains, planner limits, or velocity references as part of adopting this formulation. A change of formulation and a change of tuning must not be measured together.
  • No coordinate blending inside the controller (Section 12.7).
  • No proof of recursive invariance under turning. As in the DCM formulation, heading rotation couples the error axes, and the scalar sets of Section 3 are applied per-axis as a finite-horizon contract.

docs.title: 19) Open questions
docs.text:
1. What carries the other half of the prediction bias? Partly answered: on 40 flat cruise steps, measured \(k_G\) removes \(54\%\) of the phase-\(0.50\) bias and \(57\%\) at commit. The residual \(\approx 0.12\) m/s is unexplained, and measured \(|k_{G,y}|\) is too small by two to five times to have accounted for all of it. Gate 1 asks which of the pivot offset, the effective ZMP, or an unmodelled term carries the remainder — on terrain as well as flat.
  2. How often does the cone leak? Section 4.9 argues the leak is self-penalizing and confined to acceleration, but that is an argument, not data. plan/conic_gap settles it.
  3. Does the lateral axis ever cross to the \(E_0 > 0\) branch in normal walking, and does the classifier switch cleanly when it does?
  4. Are the \(31\) mm pivot and \(103\) mm effective-ZMP terms separable, or is one absorbing a different physical effect?
  5. Is the closure-rate coefficient of (5.3) confirmed? Two measurements on opposite sides of the model, from different step populations, is suggestive, not established.
  6. Non-constant CoM height. Equation (1.1) stays exact, but the kinematic relation (1.2) and the exchange correction (2.5) both acquire \(\dot z\) terms, and \(\xi\zeta\) is no longer invariant — so the cone of Section 4.3 is then only approximately the reachable set. This formulation uses measured \(\dot z\); a planner that chooses \(H(t)\) is a larger problem.
  7. Double support is unmodelled, and matters more here than in the DCM formulation, because the terminal condition is defined at an instant that double support smears out — and because the \(L\)-conservation argument of Section 2.3 assumes a single impulsive contact.
  8. Finite-foot CoP authority. The model pins the CoP at the contact point. A real ankle gives a second, faster input to (2.6) and would change Section 6 substantially. It also completes the authority hierarchy:
\[ \text{contact forces (1 kHz)} \to \text{swing reshaping (1 kHz)} \to r_k\ (50\ \mathrm{Hz}) \to T_1\ (50\ \mathrm{Hz}) \to \text{route (slow)}. \]

docs.text: Every number in this document that is not derived from Section 1.7's constants is measured. This section records where each came from, so that the body text can be read without following a reference, and so that a reader who doubts a number knows exactly what to re-run.

docs.title: 20.3) Recorded failures cited as constraints
docs.text:
These are not measurements of the robot; they are outcomes of prior attempts, cited because each one is the reason a rule in this document is stated as a rule rather than a preference.

docs.title: DCM Footstep Planner Formulation (Progress Tracking + Heading)
docs.text: This deep reference explains the DCM model, heading-aware geometry and alternative optimization formulations. Its current implementation is the C++ locomotion::dcm::DcmPlanner, alongside the independent ALIP kernel. The module contract, kernel implementation and Digit profile own the actual API and assembled problem.

docs.title: Current implementation map
docs.text:
Topic Current C++ behavior Retained derivation or alternative Model and heading Constant-height DCM; desired heading precomputed outside the QP; yaw-rate and absolute-target commands Section 1 derives the shared dynamics and frames Timing and cadence First-step timing optimized before commitment; command-scaled planar reference cadence is unconditional The former command_scaled_reference_gait switch is retired Objective Six authorable weights: length, width, width symmetry, timing, progress and lateral Python gait-smoothness, operating-envelope and swing weights are retired Geometry and viability Hard physical gait and correct-side topology rows; viability slacks have an exact-penalty weight, with explicit stopping/recovery handling The two-envelope hard/soft program below is the retired Python variant, not the current matrix layout Swing capability No swing-speed or swing-acceleration rows The swing-capability derivation is an uninstalled alternative Terminal storage A reserved coordinate and final rows remain pinned/inactive to preserve the established numerical layout The old terminal schedule is not an authorable controller feature Terrain extensions Current numerical solve remains planar Disjoint-region MIQP and variable-height sections are mathematical extensions, not deployed terrain capability

The Python implementation was retired on 2026-09-18. Its two-envelope QP remains here to explain the modeling choices and comparisons; sections that describe it are labeled accordingly. The current C++ solver does not have a maintained Python/CVXPY parity backend. Numerical feasibility does not certify swing tracking, controller feasibility, persistent-turn invariance or physical recovery.

The current Digit profile allows 0.30–0.60 s solver duration, with a separate 0.42–0.48 s reference cadence band. The walking coordinator owns lifecycle and installed-command admission; the numerical kernel does not own a Servo gait state machine.

docs.title: 1.1) DCM definition (flat terrain)
docs.text:
In LIPM-like walking with constant CoM height, define the DCM (a.k.a. capture point)

\[ z \;=\; x_c + \frac{1}{\lambda}\dot{x}_c,\qquad \lambda = \sqrt{\frac{g}{z_c}}. \]

We plan in the horizontal plane, so \(z_k, p_k \in \mathbb{R}^2\).

docs.title: 1.2) Step-indexed variables
docs.text:
At (touchdown of) step \(k\):

  • DCM: \(z_k \in \mathbb{R}^2\)
  • Stance foot position: \(p_k \in \mathbb{R}^2\)
  • Desired heading (world yaw): \(\theta_k \in \mathbb{R}\). This is the state of the command-side heading generator, not the measured yaw of the stance foot or robot body.

Store this state on an unwrapped real line so repeated turns remain continuous. The retired Python command integrated scalar yaw rate directly and therefore computes no wrapped target-angle error.

  • Stance flag: \(l_k \in \{0,1\}\) with
  • \(l_k = 0\) = right stance
  • \(l_k = 1\) = left stance
  • stance sign: \(s_k := (-1)^{l_k} \in \{+1,-1\}\)

Conventions: some earlier drafts use the opposite encoding for left/right stance. All formulas in this note assume \(l_k=0\) (right) and \(l_k=1\) (left).

  • Step displacement (world frame): $$ u_k^w := p_{k+1}^w - p_k^w \in \mathbb{R}^2. $$
  • Step duration \(T_k\) encoded by timing factor $$ \sigma_k := e^{\lambda T_k} \in [\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}],\qquad \sigma_{\min} > 1. $$ On flat terrain with constant \(\lambda\), these bounds correspond to $$ \sigma_{\min} = e^{\lambda T_{\min}},\qquad \sigma_{\max} = e^{\lambda T_{\max}}. $$

The stance alternates:

\[ l_{k+1} = 1 - l_k,\qquad s_{k+1} = -s_k. \]

docs.title: 1.3) Desired-world-heading solve chart (pre-computed per solve)
docs.text:
Rotation from desired-heading coordinates (forward/left) to world:

\[ R( heta) = egin{bmatrix} \cos heta & -\sin heta\ \sin heta & \cos heta \end{bmatrix}. \]

At each admitted touchdown, freeze one solve chart with measured translation and planner-owned orientation:

\[ o_1^w:=p_1^w, \qquad Q_1:=R( heta_1), \qquad \widetilde r:=Q_1^ op(r^w-o_1^w). \]

Thus \(\widetilde p_1=0\). Every preview foothold and DCM node in that solve uses this same chart; predicted nodes are not re-originated. From here onward, unless a world superscript is shown, \(p_k\) and \(z_k\) denote these solve-chart coordinates and the tilde is dropped. The DCM dynamics are unchanged by this rigid coordinate change.

Accordingly, from this point forward

\[ u_k:=p_{k+1}-p_k=Q_1^ op u_k^w. \]

Define relative node headings

\[ \delta_k:= heta_k- heta_1, \qquad \delta_1=0. \]

The corresponding desired-heading axes in the solve chart are

\[ \hat{x}_k := egin{bmatrix}\cos\delta_k\ \sin\delta_k\end{bmatrix}, \qquad \hat{y}_k := egin{bmatrix}-\sin\delta_k\ \cos\delta_k\end{bmatrix}. \]

Equivalently, the world axes remain the columns of \(R( heta_k)\).

For turning, express each step in the frame at the midpoint of its two endpoint headings. Define

\[ \alpha_k := heta_{k+1}- heta_k, \qquad ar\delta_k := \delta_k + rac{\alpha_k}{2}, \]

and let \(\hat x_{k+1/2},\hat y_{k+1/2}\) be the columns of \(R( ar\delta_k)\) in the solve chart, or \(R( heta_k+\alpha_k/2)\) in world. The desired-heading step coordinates are

\[ u_k := R( ar\delta_k)^ op u_k = egin{bmatrix} u_k^x\ u_k^y \end{bmatrix} = egin{bmatrix} \hat{x}_{k+1/2}^ op (p_{k+1}-p_k)\ \hat{y}_{k+1/2}^ op (p_{k+1}-p_k) \end{bmatrix}. \]

Equivalently in world coordinates, \( u_k=R( heta_k+\alpha_k/2)^ op u_k^w\).

The measured stance-foot translation is therefore only the chart origin. Its yaw, which can be distorted by uneven terrain, never enters \(Q_1\), \(\delta_k\), or any planned axis. At admitted touchdown, re-anchor translation at the new measured contact but advance orientation only through \( heta_1\leftarrow heta_2^{\mathrm{accepted}}\). The body and feet are downstream tracking systems: they follow the desired-world heading; they do not define it.

docs.title: 1.4) Step-to-step DCM dynamics
docs.text:
Assuming CoP is at the stance foot \(p_k\) during step \(k\), the DCM update is

\[ z_{k+1} = p_k + (z_k - p_k)\sigma_k = \sigma_k z_k + (1-\sigma_k)p_k. \]

Define DCM error w.r.t. the stance foot:

\[ e_k := z_k - p_k. \]

Then using \(p_{k+1}=p_k+u_k\),

\[ e_{k+1} = \sigma_k e_k - u_k. \]

In node desired-heading coordinates,

\[ \eta_k := R(\delta_k)^\top e_k, \]

the same update is

\[ \boxed{\; \eta_{k+1} = \sigma_k R(-\alpha_k)\eta_k - R(-\alpha_k/2)\nu_k. \;} \]

This exact coupled recursion reduces to \(\eta_{k+1}=\sigma_k\eta_k-\nu_k\) when \(\alpha_k=0\). The finite-horizon planner uses it directly; projecting the scalar straight-heading invariant envelope into a rotating preview does not claim the nonzero-heading set is invariant.

docs.title: 1.5) Simplifying assumptions
docs.text:
The following assumptions are made throughout this formulation:

  • CoP at stance foot: no ankle torque exploitation; the center of pressure is fixed at the stance foot position during each step.
  • Single support only: the double support phase is not modeled; transitions are instantaneous.
  • Point-contact / flat feet: foot rotation dynamics are not QP states; desired-yaw trajectory screening enforces the downstream acceleration limit and a rate envelope coherent with the planner's own increment/timing range.
  • Constant CoM height: the LIPM assumption \(z_c = \text{const}\) holds within each step (on flat terrain, globally; on variable-height terrain, per-step).
  • No swing-foot translation trajectory optimization: only the landing position is optimized. The mandatory yaw interpolation is constructed algebraically after the solve; swing-foot collision avoidance remains a separate downstream responsibility.
  • Pre-computed heading: the heading sequence \(\{\theta_k\}\) is fixed before the optimization to preserve linearity.

docs.title: 2) Flat terrain planner: one heading-aware QP
docs.text: The dynamics, heading construction and physical gait geometry motivate the current kernel. The complete objective and two-envelope assembly developed in this section describe the retired Python variant. Use the implementation map above to distinguish shared mathematics from optional or removed terms; do not copy its variable layout or config keys into the current C++ app.

docs.title: 2.1) Planner inputs
docs.text:
At each solve the planner receives:

  • the measured stance translation, DCM, stance side, elapsed step time, and held step duration;
  • the last admitted step's command-relative fore-aft residual, physical width, and duration (or the launch seed \(0,W_{\mathrm{nom}},T_{\mathrm{nom}}\));
  • the planner-owned accepted desired-world heading \(\theta_1\);
  • horizon, gait limits, timing limits, nominal gait, hard-set numerical tolerance, and objective weights;
  • commanded desired-heading-frame velocity \((v_x,v_y)\); and
  • one signed body yaw rate \(\omega\).

The desired heading is command state, not a measured robot frame. Session/reset initializes it from the accepted app state. An app or upstream navigation source that wants to face an absolute world heading owns that feedback law and supplies a yaw rate before this boundary; measured body and stance-foot yaw are downstream tracking feedback only.

All finite translational and heading commands proceed to the same QP after structural validation and increment clamping. There is no velocity-domain or turning-profile certification gate. The accepted-plan governor may report a realized translational velocity no larger than the request, but it does not pre-certify \(v_x\) or \(v_y\) as a condition for turning.

docs.title: 2.2) Pre-compute the continuous bounded heading sequence
docs.text:
To preserve convexity, \(\theta_k\) is not a decision variable. The command-side generator builds the unwrapped desired-world sequence before QP assembly. The fixed preview duration is \(T_{\mathrm{nom}}\).

The sole maintained command rule is:

\[ \alpha_k = \operatorname{clamp}\!\left( \omega T_{\mathrm{nom}}, -\alpha_{\max}, +\alpha_{\max} \right). \]

Advance

\[ \theta_{k+1}=\theta_k+\alpha_k. \]

The increment is continuous within its clamp bounds. There is no quantization, same-sign snapping, certified table, or nonzero deadband. Zero and nonzero increments use the same generator.

Although \(\sigma_1\) is optimized, \(T_{\mathrm{nom}}\) is fixed before the QP. Therefore every \(\theta_k\), \(\alpha_k\), node/midpoint axis, rotation, and constant-twist chord remains constant in the solve. Retiming changes the reported accepted average body rate to

\[ \omega_{\mathrm{real}}=\frac{\alpha_1}{T_1}, \]

but it does not change the accepted geometric increment.

There is no special turn-in-place mode. Setting \(v_x=v_y=0\) zeros the translational reference while nonzero \(\alpha_k\) rotates the same alternating-step gait.

At an accepted touchdown, advance the persistent heading only through \(\theta_1\leftarrow\theta_2^{\mathrm{accepted}}\). Re-anchor chart translation at the measured new stance contact, but never re-anchor chart orientation from measured foot or body yaw. The accepted payload carries the heading sequence. The consuming application owns its body and foot orientation trajectories.

docs.title: 2.3) Decision variables (flat terrain)
docs.text:
For a horizon of \(N\) steps, the decision variables are

\[ \{p_k\}_{k=2}^{N+1},\qquad \{z_k\}_{k=2}^{N+1},\qquad \sigma_1,\qquad \rho,\qquad \{\varepsilon_k^x,\varepsilon_k^y\}_{k=1}^{N}\ge0,\qquad \varepsilon_{\mathrm{sw}}\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^2. \]

\(\varepsilon_k^x\) and \(\varepsilon_k^y\) are meter-valued excursions outside the nominal-cadence operating envelope. They do not relax the outer viable set. \(\rho\in[0,1]\) is the existing terminal schedule relaxation; its upper bound is set to zero when the terminal schedule is disabled. \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sw}}\) relaxes only the preferred swing acceleration band, never the hard swing capability rows. Thus the implemented problem has \(6N+4\) scalar decision variables.

The current-step timing \(\sigma_1\) is optimized on every precommit solve. Future timing is fixed at the authored nominal preview duration:

\[ \sigma_k \equiv \sigma_{\mathrm{preview}} = e^{\lambda T_{\mathrm{preview}}}, \qquad k=2,\dots,N. \]

This preserves a convex QP because \(\sigma_1\) appears in the \(k=1\) dynamics only where \((z_1,p_1)\) are known constants. Optimizing future timing would make the recursion bilinear; see Section 2.8.

docs.title: 2.4) Objective: cumulative progress tracking
docs.text:
The retired Python objective assigned one owner to each behavior. Cumulative prefix progress tracks the commanded fore-aft displacement, complete-cycle cumulative progress tracks lateral translation, and width terms shape the alternating gait. The hard first-successor controlled-invariant set closes DCM feedback around the one preview state that receding-horizon execution actually reaches. Two high-priority quadratic slack costs discourage leaving the nominal DCM envelope or exceeding the preferred swing acceleration. Hard reach, width, swing-capability, dynamics, and outer-envelope rows remain the final authority.

There is deliberately no separate per-step length objective. It would track the same command as cumulative progress while giving equal importance to deeper preview steps that this MPC will discard. There is likewise no fixed one-step, all-preview, or two-step DCM-periodicity cost. Section 2.4.4 explains why capturability is enforced as a reachable set rather than attraction to one arbitrarily selected walking orbit.

docs.title: 2.4.1) Gait geometry
docs.text:
Define the step width in the desired-heading midpoint frame (always positive):

\[ W_k := s_k \nu_k^y. \]

The absolute width-shaping cost is

\[ J_{\text{width}} = \sum_{k=1}^{N} w_w(W_k - W_{\text{nom}})^2. \]

This term regulates nominal stance width. For lateral translation and turning, Section 2.4.1.2 removes the commanded body chord and heading geometry before evaluating physical width. The old preview-only adjacent-width term is replaced by the admitted-step smoothness cost in Section 2.4.5, so the first action is not left unregularized at every receding-horizon solve.

docs.title: 2.4.1.1) The reference gait, and the stride/cadence preferences
docs.text:
Retired Python implementation, 2026-09-05. The coherent command-scaled reference gait derived below was implemented in the retired Python kernel as dcm_planar_reference_gait, behind planner.command_scaled_reference_gait. It resolves one \((L_{\text{ref}}, W_{\text{ref}}, T_{\text{ref}})\) per solve and supplies it wherever the solve predicts rather than decides: deeper preview DCM propagation, the heading increment, the preview command chords, the preview swing reach, the soft operating envelope, and the launch smoothness seed. It changes no hard row -- \(\sigma_1\) still ranges over the whole timing interval and the hard \(T_{\min}\) envelope is still evaluated at \(\sigma_{\min}\).

The two objective halves, an absolute stride preference and the timing target \(w_\sigma(\sigma_1-\sigma_{\text{ref}})^2\), are present as weights.reference_length and weights.reference_timing and both default to zero.

Digit ships the whole mechanism disabled, on a matched measurement rather than on the analysis below: enabling it takes flat vx=1.0 from 11 admitted steps to 6, and flat vx=0.20 from zero high-severity support-force findings to four. See the reference-gait entry and, for the objective halves, the timing-reference ablation.

The rest of this section is the derivation and the historical rationale for why an independent stride and timing pair is the wrong shape. That part is unchanged and still governs.

The legacy choice \(L_{\text{nom}} = v_{\text{des}} T_{\text{nom}}\) together with \(w_\sigma(\sigma_1-\sigma_{\text{nom}})^2\) creates two independent set points. The first grows with the command; the second does not. Nothing in the objective expresses speed as \(L/T\), so raising \(v_{\text{des}}\) is met entirely by a longer stride, and cadence moves only when the hard row \(|\nu^x|\le L_{\max}\) makes that impossible. Measured on a speed sweep (\(L_{\max}=0.5\), \(T_{\text{nom}}=0.40\), \(T_{\min}=0.30\)), \(T_1\) sits at exactly \(0.4000\) up to \(v_{\text{des}}=1.2\) and then jumps to \(0.3137\) once the stride pins to \(L_{\max}\). One authority is spent before the other is touched, and the handover is a discontinuity.

These values are a pre-solve objective preference, not the optimized plan and not the task reference ultimately sent to the controller. Making the \(k=1\) length residual timing-consistent — replacing \(L_{\text{nom}}\) with \(L_{\text{nom}} + a_v(\sigma_1-\sigma_{\text{nom}})\), which is the correct linearization of \(v_{\text{des}}T_1(\sigma_1)\) and matches what Sections 2.4.2 and 2.4.3 already do — removes the inconsistency but changes nothing: a term that tracks speed is degenerate along the iso-speed line, and \(w_\sigma\) resolves the degeneracy straight back to \(\sigma_{\text{nom}}\).

The coherent command-dependent gait preference below is the one that was implemented. It uses the spatial range \([0,L_{\max}]\) and the temporal range \([T_{\min},T_{\text{nom}}]\) in equal proportion. Let \(r\) be their shared normalized utilization:

\[ \boxed{\; r(v_{\mathrm{des}}^g) =\frac{|v_{\mathrm{des}}^g|\,T_{\text{nom}}} {L_{\max}+|v_{\mathrm{des}}^g|\,(T_{\text{nom}}-T_{\min})}, \qquad L_{\text{pref}}=\operatorname{sign}(v_{\mathrm{des}}^g)\,r\,L_{\max}, \qquad T_{\text{pref}}=T_{\text{nom}}-r\,(T_{\text{nom}}-T_{\min}). \;} \]

\(r\) is precisely the value that makes \(L_{\text{pref}}/T_{\text{pref}}=v_{\mathrm{des}}^g\) — solve \(rL_{\max}=|v_{\mathrm{des}}^g| \big(T_{\text{nom}}-r(T_{\text{nom}}-T_{\min})\big)\) and restore the sign through \(L_{\mathrm{pref}}=\operatorname{sign}(v_{\mathrm{des}}^g)rL_{\max}\) — so the preference is a coherent gait nominal rather than a pair of unrelated set points, and both quantities move continuously with the command. \(r=1\) occurs exactly at \(|v_{\mathrm{des}}^g|=L_{\max}/T_{\min}\), so the two authorities saturate at the same speed. The governance in Section 2.1 guarantees \(r\in[0,1]\); a defensive clamp is allowed only with the same reported saturation and governed value, never while publishing the raw velocity. At \(v_{\mathrm{des}}^g=0\) it degenerates correctly to \(L_{\text{pref}}=0\), \(T_{\text{pref}}=T_{\text{nom}}\).

At \(L_{\max}=0.75\), \(T_{\text{nom}}=0.40\), \(T_{\min}=0.30\):

\(v_x\) \(L_{\text{pref}}\) \(T_{\text{pref}}\) reserve \(1-r\) 0.4 0.152 m 0.380 s 80% 0.8 0.289 m 0.361 s 61% 1.2 0.414 m 0.345 s 45% 1.6 0.527 m 0.330 s 30% 2.0 0.632 m 0.316 s 16% 2.5 0.750 m 0.300 s 0%

\(T_{\text{pref}}\) then replaces \(T_{\text{nom}}\) consistently in the timing anchor, preview DCM propagation \(\sigma_{\text{pref}}=e^{\lambda T_{\text{pref}}}\), translational preferences, and heading increment. The bounds of Section 2.5(c) separately use the fresh-step timing range because the next executed step retimes when replanned.

\(\sigma_1\) remains a decision variable around this preference. Its nominal gait range is \([\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}]\), while the authoritative online interval is \([\sigma_1^{\mathrm{lo}},\max(\sigma_1^{\mathrm{lo}},\sigma_{\max})]\) from Section 2.5(a.1). Thus the usual range is unchanged until the elapsed-time floor overtakes it; after that, the \(T_{\max}\) preference deliberately yields to causality. Nothing here adds a decision variable: every affected preference quantity is a constant of the solve, and the problem stays a convex QP.

Measured on the same sweep, each configuration started from its own steady state: stride and cadence both move from the first speed, commanded speed is tracked exactly through \(1.2\) m/s, and \(L_{\max}\) saturation moves from \(v_x=1.6\) to \(v_x=2.0\) against an unchanged \(L_{\max}/T_{\min}\) ceiling — the reserve costs no top speed.

The deferred C++ backend retains a private command-scaled resolver. The retired Python backend did not use that output or expose those preferences as objective weights.

docs.title: 2.4.1.2) Exact constant-twist preference in the midpoint frame
docs.text:
For each fixed, pre-computed increment \(\alpha_k\), define

\[ \gamma_k:=\operatorname{sinc}\!\left( rac{\alpha_k}{2} ight), \qquad \operatorname{sinc}(x):= egin{cases} \sin x/x,&x e0,\ 1,&x=0, \end{cases} \]

and integrate the commanded desired-body/tangent-frame translational velocity over the fixed preview duration:

\[ oxed{ d_k:=\gamma_k T_{\mathrm{nom}} egin{bmatrix}v_{\mathrm{des}}\v_y\end{bmatrix}. } \]

This is the exact constant-body-twist chord expressed in the edge-midpoint heading frame. It is the planner's progress target. An application trajectory need not use constant twist as its instantaneous time law; this chord is an objective target, not an executed reference. If the nominal feet lie at lateral offsets \(\mp W_{\mathrm{nom}}/2\) from the desired body path, the corresponding footstep preference is

\[ oxed{ u_k^{\mathrm{pref}} =d_k+ egin{bmatrix}0\s_kW_{\mathrm{nom}}\cos(\alpha_k/2)\end{bmatrix}. } \]

Define the physical-width proxy

\[ \overline W_k:= rac{s_k( u_k^y-d_k^y)}{\cos(\alpha_k/2)}. \]

The bounded increment must keep

\[ \cos(\alpha_k/2)>0 \]

with a numerical floor, so the physical-width proxy remains well conditioned. The heading-aware absolute width cost is

\[ J_{\mathrm{width}} =\sum_{k=1}^{N}w_w(\overline W_k-W_{\mathrm{nom}})^2. \]

For the executed step only, make \(d_1\) timing-aware without changing \(\alpha_1\):

\[ T_1^{\mathrm{lin}}(\sigma_1) :=T_c + rac{\sigma_1-\sigma_c} {\lambda\sigma_c}, \qquad d_1(\sigma_1) :=\gamma_1T_1^{\mathrm{lin}}(\sigma_1) egin{bmatrix}v_{\mathrm{des}}\v_y\end{bmatrix}. \]

Here \(\sigma_c\) is the midpoint of the currently admissible growth-factor interval and \(T_c=\log(\sigma_c)/\lambda\). All rotations and trigonometric factors remain constants of the solve, while \(d_1\) is affine in \(\sigma_1\). The progress objective therefore remains convex quadratic. With \(v_{\mathrm{des}}=v_y=0\), the same preference produces ordinary alternating steps around a stationary desired body path; no turn-in-place mode exists.

The chord is exact at fixed \(T_{\mathrm{nom}}\) for future steps; the current-step duration correction is first order in \(\sigma_1\), not an exact evaluation of \(\log\sigma_1\). For the active feasible timing interval, record

\[ \epsilon_T^{\mathrm{lin}} :=\max_{\sigma\in[\sigma_1^{\mathrm{lo}},\sigma_1^{\mathrm{hi}}]} \left| rac{\log\sigma}{\lambda}-T_1^{\mathrm{lin}}(\sigma) ight|, \]

which occurs at an interval endpoint. Declare and validate the operating range over which this objective approximation is acceptable. Outside that range, report degraded velocity-preference accuracy rather than claiming exact current-step constant-twist chord evaluation. This approximation changes no hard dynamics or viability row.

docs.title: 2.4.2) Cumulative forward progress tracking
docs.text:
This was the retired Python planner's mean fore-aft displacement-tracking objective. Cumulative progress makes later preview steps react to an earlier preview deficit and naturally gives the executed first action the greatest weight. The hard first-successor invariant set separately closes DCM-state feedback. This term is not cross-solve integral action.

Define the cumulative desired-heading forward displacement from step 1:

\[ F_k := \sum_{i=1}^{k-1} \nu_i^x = \sum_{i=1}^{k-1} \hat{x}_{i+1/2}^\top(p_{i+1} - p_i), \qquad k = 2,\dots,N+1. \]

Using the constant-twist chords from Section 2.4.1.2, the timing-aware reference progress is

\[ F_k^{\text{des}}(\sigma_1) :=d_1^x(\sigma_1)+\sum_{i=2}^{k-1}d_i^x, \qquad k=2,\dots,N+1. \]

The progress tracking cost:

\[ J_{\text{progress}} = \sum_{k=2}^{N+1} w_F\left(F_k - F_k^{\text{des}}(\sigma_1)\right)^2. \]

Key properties:

  • Within-horizon deficit compensation (not cross-step integral action). Let \(\epsilon_i:=\nu_i^x-d_i^x\). Then \(F_k-F_k^{\text{des}}=\sum_{i<k}\epsilon_i\), so within a single solve a short early step is felt by every later term. This does not accumulate across solves. \(F_k\) is measured from the current \(p_1\), so it resets at every touchdown and the planner carries no commanded-versus-realized progress state. Genuine integral action would require such a state, and on a divergent plant it would also require its own anti-windup treatment; neither is specified here. Do not read this term as eliminating steady-state position error.
  • Natural time-discounting. Step 1's error appears in all \(N\) terms; step \(N\)'s error appears in only 1 term. This is appropriate for an MPC that executes only step 1.
  • Timing coupling. \(d_1(\sigma_1)\) adjusts the reference when the optimizer changes current-step duration.
  • Convexity. \(F_k\) is linear in \(\{p_k\}\) and \(F_k^{\text{des}}\) is linear in \(\sigma_1\), so \(J_{\text{progress}}\) is convex quadratic. Cross-terms between \(p_k\) and \(\sigma_1\) appear in the Hessian but the QP structure is preserved.

docs.title: 2.4.3) Lateral velocity (when \(v_y \neq 0\))
docs.text:
Lateral velocity arises from the body-chord component \(d_k^y\). Remove the nominal rotating foot offset from each step:

\[ \chi_k^y:=\nu_k^y-s_kW_{\mathrm{nom}}\cos(\alpha_k/2), \]

Only complete same-foot cycles are compared, because a single foot-to-foot step contains the alternating stance-width offset. For cycle endpoint \(m\in\{2,4,\ldots,2\lfloor N/2\rfloor\}\), define

\[ C_m^y:=\sum_{k=1}^{m}\chi_k^y, \qquad C_m^{y,\mathrm{des}}(\sigma_1):= d_1^y(\sigma_1)+\sum_{k=2}^{m}d_k^y. \]

The Digit application additionally supplies one bounded carried error \(E_y\) in meters. Its sign convention is requested minus measured lateral progress over completed same-foot cycles. The QP residual and cost are

\[ \boxed{ r_m^y=C_m^y-C_m^{y,\mathrm{des}}(\sigma_1)-E_y, \qquad J_{\text{lat}}=w_{\text{lat}}\sum_{m\in\{2,4,\ldots\}}(r_m^y)^2. } \]

Thus a positive realized deficit asks the QP to plan the missing progress once; it does not alter the private gait preference before problem construction.

At the application boundary, after a newly admitted transition closes a same-foot cycle,

\[ E_y^+ =\operatorname{clip}\!\left( E_y+\Delta y_{\mathrm{requested}}-\Delta y_{\mathrm{measured}}, -(W_{\max}-W_{\min}), +(W_{\max}-W_{\min}) \right). \]

Requested and measured displacements are integrated on the same control-tick intervals in the accepted desired-heading chart. The state resets on session reset, zero lateral command, or command-sign reversal. There is no enable flag, filter coefficient, integral gain, or pre-QP displacement correction. The geometry-derived clip is anti-windup; hard width and viability rows remain the final authority if the requested make-up progress is infeasible.

When \(v_y = 0\), all lateral body-chord reference displacements vanish, the carried state is reset, and width regulation in \(J_{\text{width}}\) drives symmetric stepping.

docs.title: 2.4.4) Capturability feedback without a fixed periodic point
docs.text:
Velocity progress alone does not constrain the unstable step-to-step DCM state, while driving DCM error to zero would describe standing capture rather than commanded walking. The maintained planner therefore closes DCM feedback with the reachable sets in Section 2.5(c), not with a preferred point:

  • the reconstructed current state must lie in the hard \(T_{\min}\) controlled-invariant envelope;
  • the executable successor \((e_2^x,q_2)\) must remain in that same hard set; and
  • slacks against the inner \(T_{\mathrm{nom}}\) envelope measure and penalize loss of ordinary-cadence capture reserve.

This admits the family of walking states that can be continued by a legal step. Width preference, cumulative commanded progress, and admitted-step smoothness select among those states. There is no authored lateral DCM center, contraction pole, or Poincare-map residual in the QP objective.

The hard row applies only to the successor that can execute before replanning. Deeper preview timing is fixed at \(T_{\mathrm{nom}}\) and those nodes are discarded. Requiring the final preview node to enter the nominal envelope would reject some states near the valid \(T_{\min}\) capture boundary even though a new solve at the first successor can select another legal duration. A hard terminal capture set would require either controllable future timing or a backward- reachable set derived for the fixed preview cadence; neither is claimed here.

docs.title: 2.4.5) Admitted-step gait smoothness
docs.text:
The MPC executes only its first step and discards the rest of the preview at the next support exchange. Adjacent-preview differences alone therefore do not penalize the discontinuity between the action that was just executed and the new first action. Define the command-relative fore-aft correction

\[ r_k^x:=\nu_k^x-d_k^x \]

and let \((r_{\mathrm{prev}}^x,\overline W_{\mathrm{prev}},T_{\mathrm{prev}})\) be the last admitted step. The application advances this boundary only after contact admission and holds it fixed through every replan in the new step. At launch it is initialized to

\[ (r_{\mathrm{prev}}^x,\overline W_{\mathrm{prev}},T_{\mathrm{prev}}) =(0,W_{\mathrm{nom}},T_{\mathrm{nom}}). \]

For the preview sequences, define boundary-seeded differences

\[ \Delta r_1^x=r_1^x-r_{\mathrm{prev}}^x, \qquad \Delta r_k^x=r_k^x-r_{k-1}^x,\quad k=2,\dots,N, \] \[ \Delta \overline W_1=\overline W_1-\overline W_{\mathrm{prev}}, \qquad \Delta \overline W_k=\overline W_k-\overline W_{k-1}, \quad k=2,\dots,N, \]

and, because only the first duration is an online decision,

\[ \Delta T_1=T_1^{\mathrm{lin}}(\sigma_1)-T_{\mathrm{prev}}. \]

One public dimensionless weight acts on the three physically normalized residuals:

\[ \boxed{ J_{\mathrm{smooth}}=w_{\mathrm{smooth}}\left[ \sum_{k=1}^{N}\left(\frac{\Delta r_k^x}{L_{\max}}\right)^2 +\sum_{k=1}^{N}\left( \frac{\Delta\overline W_k}{W_{\max}-W_{\min}} \right)^2 +\left(\frac{\Delta T_1}{T_{\max}-T_{\min}}\right)^2 \right]. } \]

This is action regularization, not a periodic-orbit or Lyapunov objective. It does not restore an absolute per-step length or timing target, and it cannot by itself prove contraction of the step-to-step DCM map.

docs.title: 2.4.6) Soft operating-envelope penalty
docs.text:
The outer invariant envelope in Section 2.5(c) is hard. Inside it, the maintained implementation gives the narrower nominal-cadence envelope a soft quadratic penalty:

\[ J_{\mathrm{env}}=w_{\mathrm{env}}\sum_{k=1}^{N} \left[(\varepsilon_k^x)^2+(\varepsilon_k^y)^2\right]. \]

This is a soft-constraint penalty, not a DCM-periodicity target. It selects a preferred region without choosing a nominal point inside that region, and it does not change the outer hard feasible set.

docs.title: 2.4.7) Swing operating penalty
docs.text:
Section 2.5(d) defines nonnegative per-axis slacks \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sw}}\) on the preferred swing-acceleration band. Their penalty is

\[ J_{\mathrm{swing}}=w_{\mathrm{swing}} \lVert\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sw}}\rVert_2^2. \]

The physical swing-acceleration and mean-speed rows remain hard. This soft inner row is what lets the QP trade stride against the current-step duration without an authored cadence target.

docs.title: 2.4.8) Complete objective
docs.text:
\[ J = J_{\text{width}} + J_{\text{progress}} + J_{\text{lat}} + J_{\text{smooth}} + J_{\text{env}} + J_{\text{swing}} + w_\rho\rho + J_{\text{ridge}}. \]

Every width/progress/smoothness/slack residual above is affine in \((p_k,z_k,\sigma_1)\) after \(\{\alpha_k\}\) is selected. Consequently the complete objective remains convex quadratic for straight walking, translating turns, and turn-in-place. The terminal relaxation is linear, and the small relative ridge keeps every solver variable in a positive-definite Hessian block.

Interpretation: with zero translational command, \(d_k=0\) and the robot uses the same alternating gait to turn in place. With nonzero translation, the constant-twist chord makes the reference follow the commanded arc. The forward cumulative term discourages deficit only within the current horizon. Lateral cumulative tracking additionally receives the bounded cross-solve same-foot progress error from Section 2.4.3.

docs.title: (a) DCM dynamics (QP with first-step timing only)
docs.text:
For the current step:

\[ z_{2} = \sigma_{1} z_1 + (1-\sigma_{1})p_1. \]

For the remaining horizon (fixed reference timing), for \(k=2,\dots,N\):

\[ z_{k+1} = \sigma_{\text{pref}} z_k + (1-\sigma_{\text{pref}})p_k. \]

docs.title: (a.1) Elapsed-time floor on the current-step timing
docs.text:
\(\sigma_1\) encodes the total duration \(T_1\) of the current step, measured from its own touchdown — not the remaining swing time. A solve issued at elapsed time \(\tilde t\) must therefore never command \(T_1 < \tilde t\), which would place the landing in the past. The static bound \(\sigma_{\min} \le \sigma_1\) does not express this: once \(\tilde t > T_{\min}\) it admits landing times that have already elapsed.

Impose instead

\[ \boxed{\; \sigma_1^{\text{lo}} := \max\big(\sigma_{\min},\; e^{\lambda(\tilde t + \Delta T)}\big) \;\le\; \sigma_1 \;\le\; \sigma_1^{\text{hi}} := \max\big(\sigma_1^{\text{lo}},\; \sigma_{\max}\big), \qquad \Delta T \ge 0 . \;} \]

Key properties:

  • Causality. \(\Delta T = 0\) recovers the minimal requirement \(T_1 \ge \tilde t\): the step may end now, but not earlier.
  • Executable-policy reserve. The equality case is an algebraic limit. A composing robot profile chooses \(\Delta T>0\) so its swing policy has a finite remaining interval.
  • Executable reserve. \(\Delta T > 0\) additionally reserves a minimum remaining swing time, so a consumer is not handed a landing time its swing policy cannot reach. Choose \(\Delta T\) as the shortest swing segment the foot controller can traverse.
  • The ceiling yields, not causality. When \(\tilde t + \Delta T\) overruns \(T_{\max}\), \(\sigma_1^{\text{hi}}\) rises to meet the floor. An earlier draft clamped the floor down to \(\sigma_{\max}\) instead, which returns \(T_1 < \tilde t\) — a landing already in the past — and preserves neither causality nor the promised swing reserve. \(T_{\max}\) is a gait-shape preference; causality is not, so the preference is what gives way. The scalar timing interval stays nonempty either way; its coupling through dynamics and hard gait/viability rows can still make the full QP infeasible.
  • Soft self-commitment. The floor meets a candidate duration when \(\tilde t+\Delta T=T_1\). Thus the available retiming window closes as the reserved landing time approaches, not necessarily only as \(\tilde t\to T_1\). Section 2.7 makes that closure explicit and extends it to landing position and desired touchdown heading.
  • Not a commitment. The floor moves with \(\tilde t\) but leaves \(\sigma_1\) free above it. Timing is re-optimized at every solve; freezing it for the duration of a step would remove the cheapest and fastest disturbance response the planner has.

docs.title: (b) Kinematic feasibility (desired-heading midpoint frame)
docs.text:
For \(k=1,\dots,N\):

\[ -L_{\max} \le \hat{x}_{k+1/2}^\top(p_{k+1}-p_k) \le L_{\max}, \] \[ W_{\min} \le s_k\,\hat{y}_{k+1/2}^\top(p_{k+1}-p_k) \le W_{\max}. \]

These constraints are linear because \(\hat{x}_{k+1/2},\hat{y}_{k+1/2}\) are pre-computed constants. They are the mathematical gait box; the online rows use the once-tightened execution bounds defined in Section 2.5(c) and formalized in Section 2.9.

They are not a swing-speed certificate. Reaching \(L_{\max}\) or \(W_{\max}\) at \(T_{\min}\) repeatedly may be infeasible for the full robot even though every landing lies in this box. A physically meaningful online swing constraint must start from the measured or currently commanded swing-foot position, velocity, and acceleration, the remaining time to touchdown, and calibrated directional velocity/acceleration limits. Those values are not part of the numerical DcmPlannerState today, so the maintained QP does not pretend that a second displacement box proves swing reachability. Adding the necessary state and calibration is a separate app-to-kernel contract change.

docs.title: (c) Hard outer invariant envelope and soft operating envelope
docs.text:
At each predicted touchdown define the desired-heading coordinates

\[ e_{k+1}^x:=\hat x_{k+1}^\top(z_{k+1}-p_{k+1}), \qquad q_{k+1}:=s_{k+1}\hat y_{k+1}^\top(z_{k+1}-p_{k+1}). \]

\(q\) is the stance-folded lateral DCM error. Negative \(q\) is permitted by the reduced model: it means the DCM is outboard of the current stance foot, but it does not permit the next foot to cross because signed step width remains an independent hard constraint. The planner has no \(q_{\mathrm{periodic}}\) field, no \(q>0\) row, and no measured-state ankle allowance.

docs.title: Timing-controlled invariant-set derivation
docs.text:
At zero heading increment, the stance-folded recursion is

\[ q^+=W-\sigma q, \qquad W\in[W_{\min},W_{\max}], \qquad \sigma\in[\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}]. \]

Seek the widest interval \([L,U]\) for which every state has at least one legal width and timing that returns the successor to the interval. At \(q=U\), the largest achievable successor uses the widest, fastest step and must reach \(L\); at \(q=L\), the smallest achievable successor uses the narrowest, fastest step and must reach \(U\). The boundary conditions are therefore

\[ W_{\max}-\sigma_{\min}U=L, \qquad W_{\min}-\sigma_{\min}L=U. \]

Solving them gives

\[ \boxed{ L(\sigma)=\frac{\sigma W_{\min}-W_{\max}}{\sigma^2-1}, \qquad U(\sigma)=\frac{\sigma W_{\max}-W_{\min}}{\sigma^2-1}. } \]

The longitudinal map \(e_x^+=\sigma e_x-u_x\) with \(|u_x|\le L_{\max}\) has the symmetric invariant interval

\[ \boxed{ |e_x|\le B_x(\sigma), \qquad B_x(\sigma)=\frac{L_{\max}}{\sigma-1}. } \]

The ordinary timing authority is the complete interval \(\sigma\in[\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}]\). Since the least unstable factor \(\sigma_{\min}\) produces the widest invariant intervals, the hard outer envelope is

\[ \mathcal V_{\mathrm{hard}}= [-B_x(\sigma_{\min}),B_x(\sigma_{\min})] \times[L(\sigma_{\min}),U(\sigma_{\min})]. \]

This does not make \(T_{\min}\) a recovery mode. It proves the existential statement behind controlled invariance: a state on the outer boundary may need the shortest ordinary step, while an interior state may use any feasible timing. For Digit simulation \(T_{\min}=0.30\) s is ordinary solver authority, and no cost or mode switch is attached merely to selecting it.

The nominal-cadence envelope uses exactly the same equations at \(\sigma_{\mathrm{nom}}=e^{\lambda T_{\mathrm{nom}}}\):

\[ \mathcal V_{\mathrm{nom}}= [-B_x(\sigma_{\mathrm{nom}}),B_x(\sigma_{\mathrm{nom}})] \times[L(\sigma_{\mathrm{nom}}),U(\sigma_{\mathrm{nom}})]. \]

It is narrower and is imposed softly at every predicted touchdown:

\[ |e_{k+1}^x|\le B_x(\sigma_{\mathrm{nom}})+\varepsilon_k^x, \] \[ L(\sigma_{\mathrm{nom}})-\varepsilon_k^y \le q_{k+1}\le U(\sigma_{\mathrm{nom}})+\varepsilon_k^y, \qquad \varepsilon_k^x,\varepsilon_k^y\ge0. \]

These slack variables measure departure from nominal operation. They are not recovery authority and cannot weaken \(\mathcal V_{\mathrm{hard}}\).

The physical width row \(W_{\min}\le s_k\hat y_{k+1/2}^\top(p_{k+1}-p_k)\le W_{\max}\) remains separately hard. It prevents leg crossing at landing; the invariant envelope constrains the DCM state. Neither substitutes for the other.

The reconstructed initial state \((e_1^x,q_1)\) must lie in \(\mathcal V_{\mathrm{hard}}\) and is passed into the dynamics unchanged. The QP then imposes the same hard envelope on \((e_2^x,q_2)\), the only successor that will execute before the next solve. It does not impose the timing-controlled outer envelope on nodes \(k\ge3\): their timing is fixed at \(\sigma_{\mathrm{preview}}\), so doing so would silently remove the timing choice used in the invariant-set proof and can reject a valid negative \(q_1\). The soft nominal envelope still shapes every preview node. This is the receding-horizon recursive-feasibility contract.

For nonzero \(\alpha_k\), the exact two-axis recursion is coupled. The implementation applies the same scalar limits to projections in each next desired-heading frame as a finite-horizon contract; it does not claim a recursively invariant turning set.

docs.title: 2.5.1) Complete two-envelope QP (retired Python variant)
docs.text:
For every precomputed heading sequence define

\[ W_k:=s_k\hat y_{k+1/2}^\top(p_{k+1}-p_k), \] \[ e_{k+1}^x:=\hat x_{k+1}^\top(z_{k+1}-p_{k+1}), \qquad q_{k+1}:=s_{k+1}\hat y_{k+1}^\top(z_{k+1}-p_{k+1}). \]

The retired Python variant solved the following online problem

\[ \begin{aligned} \min_{\{p_k,z_k\},\,\sigma_1,\,\rho, \,\{\varepsilon_k^x,\varepsilon_k^y\}, \,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sw}}} \quad & J_{\mathrm{width}}+J_{\mathrm{progress}}+J_{\mathrm{lat}} +J_{\mathrm{smooth}}+J_{\mathrm{env}}+J_{\mathrm{swing}} +w_\rho\rho+J_{\mathrm{ridge}}\\ \text{s.t.}\quad& z_2=\sigma_1z_1+(1-\sigma_1)p_1,\\ & z_{k+1}=\sigma_{\mathrm{preview}}z_k+ (1-\sigma_{\mathrm{preview}})p_k,\quad k=2,\dots,N,\\ & -L_{\max}^{\mathrm{exec}} \le\hat x_{k+1/2}^\top(p_{k+1}-p_k) \le L_{\max}^{\mathrm{exec}},\\ & W_{\min}^{\mathrm{exec}}\le W_k\le W_{\max}^{\mathrm{exec}},\\ & B_x(\sigma_{\min})\ge |e_2^x|,\\ & L(\sigma_{\min})\le q_2\le U(\sigma_{\min}),\\ & |e_{k+1}^x|\le B_x(\sigma_{\mathrm{nom}})+\varepsilon_k^x,\\ & L(\sigma_{\mathrm{nom}})-\varepsilon_k^y \le q_{k+1}\le U(\sigma_{\mathrm{nom}})+\varepsilon_k^y,\\ & \varepsilon_k^x,\varepsilon_k^y\ge0, \qquad k=1,\dots,N,\\ & \sigma_1^{\mathrm{lo}} \le\sigma_1\le \max(\sigma_1^{\mathrm{lo}},\sigma_{\max}),\\ &0\le\rho\le\rho_{\max},\\ &\text{fixed terminal midpoint rows parameterized by }\rho,\\ &\text{hard and preferred swing-capability rows from Section 2.5(d).} \end{aligned} \]

The reconstructed initial state must independently satisfy \(|e_1^x|\le B_x(\sigma_{\min})\) and \(L(\sigma_{\min})\le q_1\le U(\sigma_{\min})\). A violation receives the explicit initial_state_outside_viable_set status; the state is not projected. The gait rows and first-successor outer envelope are hard and independently postchecked at their mathematical boundaries. Nominal-envelope slack exists in both axes but never enters those hard rows. \(\rho_{\max}=0\) disables the terminal schedule without changing graph structure; \(\rho_{\max}=1\) enables its bounded relaxation.

All heading quantities are constants, so this is a convex QP for \(\alpha_k=0\) and \(\alpha_k\ne0\) with identical dimensions. At horizon \(N\), the retired Python layout had \(6N+4\) decision variables and \(2N\) equality rows. Persistent turning and start/cruise/stop regimes change parameter values, not the problem dimensions.

That retired runtime assembled dense matrices for the repository's dual active-set QP adapter. Its cached DPP-compliant CVXPY problem and parity checks belonged to the retired implementation; they are not available reproduction commands for the current C++ kernel. A small regularization relative to the normalized physical objective remains on every variable so the active- set Hessian stays positive definite.

docs.title: 2.6) Heading-aware tracking and guarantee boundary
docs.text:
Turning is represented by the same three mechanisms for translation and turn-in-place:

  1. the command-side generator advances planner-owned world headings independently of measured foot/body yaw;
  2. gait geometry and progress use desired-heading midpoint axes and the exact constant-twist chord; and
  3. the hard outer invariant envelope is projected onto the executable successor, while the soft nominal envelope discourages operation near the outer-set boundary without selecting one periodic DCM point.

For constant nonzero \(\alpha\), define \(\omega_{\mathrm{preview}}=\alpha/T_{\mathrm{nom}}\). With \(v_y=0\), the preview chord traces the endpoint displacement of a constant-twist circle. With \(v_x=v_y=0\), the same formulation turns in place.

The guarantee is finite-horizon DCM consistency plus hard gait feasibility and one-step preservation of the straight-heading outer invariant envelope. The soft envelope is an operating preference, not a guarantee. Because heading rotation couples the error axes, this document does not claim recursive invariance for persistent turning. Integrated simulation is the current evidence boundary.

docs.title: 2.7) Late-step kernel commitment
docs.text:
The numerical kernel replans only before the configured commit phase \(\phi_c\). Before commitment, a successful solve replaces its held numerical result. At or after commitment, it bypasses optimization and republishes that held result unchanged. Bypass is a successful kernel status, not a failure.

Elapsed time and the held step duration are explicit kernel inputs. The kernel does not own a support-transition clock, swing trajectory, body-yaw trajectory, contact admission rule, or controller task. A composing application must keep those meanings coherent with the elapsed time it supplies. Resetting the kernel at an admitted support transition clears the held result so a new step cannot bypass into the previous landing.

The accepted geometric increment remains \(\alpha_1=\theta_2-\theta_1\), and the accepted average rate remains \(\omega_{\mathrm{real}}=\alpha_1/T_1\). These are numerical outputs; they do not prescribe the instantaneous orientation trajectory used by a robot controller.

docs.title: 2.8) Timing: what changes if \(\sigma_k\) is variable?
docs.text:
If you optimize \(\sigma_k\) for \(k\ge2\), the DCM dynamics

\[ z_{k+1} = \sigma_k z_k + (1-\sigma_k)p_k \]

become bilinear in decision variables \((\sigma_k,z_k,p_k)\).

Common ways to handle this:

  1. Optimize only \(\sigma_1\), fix \(\sigma\_{k\ge2}=\sigma\_{\text{pref}}\) (baseline in this note; preserves QP/MIQP structure because \((z_1,p_1)\) are constants).
  2. Convex relaxations / successive convexification (McCormick envelopes or iterative linearization) for full-horizon timing optimization.

Decision: option 1 is structural, not a default. Optimizing \(\{\sigma_k\}_{k\ge2}\) leaves the QP class — successive convexification turns a single convex solve into an iterated nonlinear program with no bounded solve time and no single feasibility certificate, neither of which a per-tick footstep planner can carry. Therefore the numerical preview fixes \(\sigma_{k\ge2}=\sigma_{\text{pref}}\).

This does not pin the closed-loop cadence. The next solve again optimizes its current step timing. Deeper fixed-cadence rows are preview regularization for both straight and turning commands; no future \(\sigma_k\) becomes an online decision variable.

The first-order linearization of step duration around \(\sigma_{\text{pref}}\) is:

\[ T_k = \frac{1}{\lambda}\log\sigma_k \approx T_{\text{pref}} + \frac{1}{\lambda\sigma_{\text{pref}}} (\sigma_k-\sigma_{\text{pref}}). \]

This is used in the progress tracking objective (Section 2.4.2) to adjust the preference when \(\sigma_1\) deviates from the command-dependent preference. In a variable-timing extension with all \(\sigma_k\) optimized, the preferred progress would need per-step timing corrections—feasible but denser in the Hessian.

docs.title: 2.9) Hard feasibility rows and soft operating rows
docs.text:
This table describes the retired two-envelope formulation. Current C++ physical gait/topology rows remain hard, while configured viability slack is separately reported and penalized. It has no soft nominal-cadence envelope or swing-capability rows.

Constraint authority is uniform across heading increments:

  • Hard: step reach, physical width, timing/input validity, DCM dynamics, initial and executable-successor outer DCM envelope, and terminal rows after their explicit schedule relaxation \(\rho\).
  • Quadratically penalized: longitudinal and lateral excursions from the nominal-cadence operating envelope.

A positive execution tightening keeps solver tolerance from weakening hard boundaries:

\[ L_{\max}^{\mathrm{exec}}=L_{\max}-\epsilon_{\mathrm{hard}}, \quad W_{\min}^{\mathrm{exec}}=W_{\min}+\epsilon_{\mathrm{hard}}, \quad W_{\max}^{\mathrm{exec}}=W_{\max}-\epsilon_{\mathrm{hard}}. \]

After solving, independently check the mathematical bounds \(|u_x|\le L_{\max}\), \(W_{\min}\le W\le W_{\max}\), and \(|e_2^x|\le B_x(\sigma_{\min})\) and \(L(\sigma_{\min})\le q_2\le U(\sigma_{\min})\). A hard-envelope violation is never accepted as a solver-tolerance convention.

The operating-envelope penalty is

\[ \min\;J+w_{\mathrm{env}}\sum_{k=1}^{N} \left[(\varepsilon_k^x)^2+(\varepsilon_k^y)^2\right], \qquad \varepsilon_k^x,\varepsilon_k^y\ge0. \]

This L2 cost is not an exact penalty. A nonzero slack reports how far a preview lies outside preferred nominal operation. It does not relax hard gait geometry or the outer invariant envelope. The full robot may have additional recovery authority through ankle torque, foot roll, or double support, but ordinary walking neither models nor spends that authority here. A separate recovery planner, with explicit physical semantics, is deferred.

Slack therefore does not make the planner unconditionally feasible. Hard gait or outer-envelope infeasibility, invalid input, solver failure, and yaw-trajectory screening can still reject a candidate.

docs.title: 2.10) Command admission, saturation, and failure handling
docs.text:
1. Validate structure and hard initial viability. Reject nonfinite state, commands, timing, or heading bounds. Reconstruct the step-start DCM and require it to lie in the outer longitudinal/lateral envelope. Negative \(q_1\) is admissible when \(q_1\ge L(\sigma_{\min})\); do not project it.
  2. Clamp heading continuously. Apply the scalar yaw-rate rule in Section 2.2. Clamping is ordinary command saturation and is reported through the selected \(\alpha\) and realized \(\alpha_1/T_1\); it is not unsupported turning.
  3. Invoke one candidate QP. Every finite bounded heading sequence uses the one row construction. No asset lookup, command cell, profile, kernel, QP bank, or fallback straight solve is consulted.
  4. Screen the result. Require a solved backend status, acceptable residual, and hard mathematical gait/outer-envelope postchecks.
  5. Retain or report failure. A failed precommit refresh leaves an already accepted result unchanged. If no initial result exists, report failure to the caller. Postcommit ticks bypass optimization and republish the held result.

Planner diagnostics distinguish solved, bypass, invalid input, degenerate bounds, initial state outside the viable set, and solver failure. They report QP dimensions, timing bounds, hard and nominal envelopes, raw initial DCM error/utilization, both nominal-envelope slacks, swing demand/slack, solver residuals, and lateral commanded/planned/residual progress. There is no unsupported-turning or asset-validation status.

docs.title: 3) Extension: stepping stones (discontinuous footholds) → MIQP
docs.text:
On stepping stones, each foot placement must lie in a union of convex regions (polytopes):

\[ \mathcal{S}^w = \bigcup_{j=1}^{M}\mathcal{S}_j^w, \qquad \mathcal{S}_j^w := \{p^w\in\mathbb{R}^2 \mid A_j^w p^w \le b_j^w\}. \]

Terrain regions are world-fixed. Because unsuperscripted \(p_k\) is a frozen solve-chart coordinate, use \(p_k^w=o_1^w+Q_1p_k\) in membership rows (or pretransform each region once into that same frozen chart).

Introduce binary region indicators \(\delta_{k j}\in\{0,1\}\) for each planned step \(k\) and region \(j\):
